context:
WillowPermit is a fictional regional licensing service adding a municipal contractor registry to its master of licensed legal organizations. Individuals trading under a personal name may be separate legal persons from a company they own. The existing master contains 310,000 records from two agencies. The new feed contains 80,000 records with a field named business_id, a source-local row key, postal addresses and effective dates. Documentation does not yet say whether business_id is national, municipality-scoped, reused, or assigned to a permit rather than an organization.

The current pipeline treats all identifier-string agreements as strong evidence, merges accepted edges by connected components, then chooses the most recently ingested address as the master address. Feed order is not the same as event time. The onboarding team cites a lower null rate as proof that the new source will improve entity accuracy. Its only manual sample is 70 records selected from a problematic municipality. Review capacity is 120 records, and access is limited to the service's controlled workspace. The task permits a shadow evaluation plan, not importing or merging records.

Describe the intake facts and contracts needed before connecting this source. Compare a conservative baseline with an alternative, separating candidate generation, identifier evidence, membership and master-field provenance. Cover source/time validity, abstention, deletion or correction response, representative versus targeted monitoring, and source-specific harms. Define a reversible pilot and success/failure/inconclusive criteria; do not fill in the unknown namespace or identity semantics merely to make the plan executable.
title: WillowPermit registry addition
